cases.evidence_note: The 2021 Court of Appeal documented material disclosure and investigation failures in Horizon-dependent prosecutions and quashed 39 appeals; this test is a period, not a fabricated exact date for any single prosecution.
The 2019 Raad van State ruling examined a 2010 benefit year's 2011/2017 administrative decisions and directed renewed recovery consideration. It did not certify any eventual cash refund.
The 4 August 2021 Raad van State judgment cites the 2019 recovery-proportionality precedent, considers hardship and special circumstances, but upholds recovery in that distinct child-budget case.

The official signed June 30 PPK replacement and matching SD e-catalog order have not been obtained; conflicting reported accounts remain unverified. A documentary gap is not proof that the authority never existed.

Analytical negative-control scenario only: misusing an HPS reference to calculate a criminal state-loss amount would contradict the 2018 regulatory text. No actual calculation in this case is adjudicated here.

An explicitly hypothetical courtroom-disclosure counterexample connected to Indonesian Chromebook trial reporting. No claim is made that prosecutors withheld material or that UK procedure applies in Indonesia.

instruments.description: Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996, Section 3, imposed prosecutor disclosure obligations. Hamilton later found failures to investigate and disclose matters undermining Horizon prosecutions.
instruments.control_action: Require prosecutors to disclose material potentially undermining the allegation, including known material software reliability problems, before relying on the system-generated shortfall.
instruments.version_limit_note: Different original and post-April-2005 disclosure tests apply depending on investigation date; current section 3 text cannot be mechanically backdated unchanged.
missing_implementation_proof: Case-specific inquiry and unused-material disclosure schedules showing what was given to each accused
Historical investigation start dates establishing which statutory wording applied

instruments.description: Article 3:4 Awb provided administrative proportionality from 1994. Its relevance to discretion under Article 26 Awir was expressly reinterpreted in the 2019 childcare-recovery judgment.
instruments.control_action: Before deciding recovery, weigh the directly affected interests and consider whether special circumstances warrant a reduction or waiver, subject to applicable sector legislation.
instruments.version_limit_note: The Article 3:4 norm predated the historical decisions, but the particular anti-automatic-recovery reading of Article 26 was not adopted by the Raad van State until 23 October 2019.
missing_implementation_proof: Original administrative decision's recorded interest balancing and explanation
Historical decision's legal interpretation, applicable Awir version and available discretion

instruments.description: The Raad van State's October 2019 ECLI:NL:RVS:2019:3536 clarified that Article 26 Awir did not invariably require full recovery, permitting mitigation in special circumstances.
instruments.control_action: Apply the court-recognized discretion to review recovery proportionality with case-specific facts and record a reasoned outcome, including when no reduction is warranted.
instruments.version_limit_note: This is an authoritative 2019 judicial interpretation, not an independently verified new statute that can prevent an earlier 2017 decision.
missing_implementation_proof: Source-specific decision reasons citing the 2019 precedent
Evidence that the claimant's special circumstances satisfied the applicable proportionality test

instruments.description: Indonesian Presidential Regulation 16/2018, Article 11, assigned PPK duties including technical procurement preparation, certain e-purchasing activity and preserving execution records.
instruments.control_action: Check PA/KPA delegation and PPK appointment dates and retain procurement documents, authority scope, and original e-purchasing records for later source-specific accountability review.
instruments.version_limit_note: The 2018 rule applies to covered public procurement, but whether a named officer was appointed for the June 2020 SD order requires signed instruments; no general automated veto is written into Article 11.
missing_implementation_proof: Signed original PPK and PA/KPA appointment/delegation instruments with effective scope
Original SD purchase order, buyer account and auditable ordering log

instruments.description: Article 26(6) Perpres 16/2018 states that the HPS estimate is not the basis for calculating state losses; this constrains what can be inferred from an estimated procurement price.
instruments.control_action: Reject any state-loss conclusion based solely on HPS; require a separate evidentiary and financial methodology before quantifying an alleged loss.
instruments.version_limit_note: The intervention is an evidentiary inference limit in the 2018 legal text, not proof that a particular state-loss assessment in the Chromebook litigation is wrong.
missing_implementation_proof: Authenticated transaction and financial records supporting an independent loss calculation
Actual judicial or audit methodology rather than an assumed HPS-price difference

instruments.description: Research-designed digital purchasing guardrail inspired by PPK authority and document-preservation duties: hold a simulated order if appointment, date, delegation or original order evidence is unverified.
instruments.control_action: On submission, validate signed PPK appointment, effective date, delegated scope and matching original order identifiers, holding any unverified transaction for human review.
instruments.version_limit_note: This is a proposed engineering control, not a legislative requirement proven operative on 30 June 2020; absence of a document in this research archive is not absence in the government's files.
missing_implementation_proof: System-level access and role management design allowing safe authorization verification
Independent records demonstrating the proposed hold control would be followed and not bypassed

instruments.description: Cross-sector governance design extrapolated from the Horizon evidentiary failure: verify independent system provenance before relying on a machine record for a consequential decision.
instruments.control_action: Require verified provenance, source audit logs, independent reviewable records, and escalation when core machine-generated evidence cannot be independently substantiated.
instruments.version_limit_note: This is a conceptual process mechanism drawn from a UK case, not an enforceable UK statute in Indonesian purchasing or a proven universal prevention intervention.
missing_implementation_proof: Actual logs, provenance and independent review capacity in the target system
Evidence that the verification would change behavior rather than merely produce a compliance checkbox

proposals.interruption_path: Disclosure of known Horizon defects could have supported challenges before unreliable data was relied on; the actual appeal found that the prosecution repeatedly failed this preexisting duty.
missing_evidence: The documentary disclosure timeline for each individual prosecution

proposals.interruption_path: An effective proportionality assessment could have identified exceptional individual hardship before full recovery; the broad statute existed, but the 2019 judicial understanding had not yet been adopted.
missing_evidence: Historical agency instructions and original reasons for 2011 and 2017 decisions

proposals.interruption_path: The 2019 interpretation justified redoing an earlier recovery decision, but could not have been a previously announced requirement preventing an already issued 2017 objection ruling.
missing_evidence: The post-remittal administrative decision and any later review

proposals.interruption_path: The 2021 appellate court expressly applied the 2019 recovery interpretation to a different child-budget dispute, assessed proportionality and still upheld recovery because relevant exceptions were not shown.
missing_evidence: Later individual administrative outcomes after the 2021 judgment

proposals.interruption_path: Retaining original delegation and PPK records would allow investigators to verify authority for an e-purchase rather than infer a signer from initials or later courtroom reporting; the originals are still unavailable.
missing_evidence: Authorized dated June 30 appointment/handover and original SD e-order matching

proposals.interruption_path: If an analyst incorrectly tried to equate HPS with state loss, Article 26(6) would block the unsupported inference; this is a synthetic review hazard, not proof such a judicial error occurred.
missing_evidence: A source-supported actual HPS and loss-accounting methodology if the issue arises

proposals.interruption_path: A proposed electronic workflow could hold a prospective purchase when signed appointment, delegated scope, timing or matching order is unverified, without claiming it was legally mandated or installed in 2020.
missing_evidence: An operator-tested workflow and historical permissions evidence

proposals.interruption_path: Transfer the general Horizon lesson about independently verifiable machine records into a proposed e-catalog provenance check; it is a governance design analogy rather than UK law imported into Indonesia.
missing_evidence: Original Indonesian technical transaction logs and operational acceptance controls

proposals.interruption_path: Independent reproducibility checks of electronic shortfalls before charge could identify defective system records if executed; no claim this proposed safeguard existed or would have changed each historic conviction.
missing_evidence: Technical reliability and independent shortfall evidence by prosecution

proposals.interruption_path: Attempting to use Dutch benefit-recovery proportionality to govern UK criminal disclosure is neither the same legal function nor enforceable domestic law, despite broad similarities in fairness principles.
UK criminal evidentiary disclosure does not regulate an Indonesian 2020 e-catalog purchase-order authorization, so this false legal transfer must be rejected rather than styled as prevention.
missing_evidence: Indonesian procurement authority, scope and primary purchase records

proposals.interruption_path: Dutch childcare-benefit recovery case law is from another jurisdiction and another administrative stage, and supplies no authority for identifying Indonesian procurement signatories.
missing_evidence: Legal applicability of Indonesian procurement regulations instead

proposals.interruption_path: A UK disclosure safeguard can suggest a research question about preserving and disclosing exculpatory technical evidence in Indonesian criminal proceedings; its statute does not bind Indonesia and no actual withholding is alleged.
missing_evidence: Original Indonesian procedural rules and the specific court's admissible evidence-disclosure orders
